text:
Alex H: FYI CI is red on master after I ran `poetry lock --no-update` to regenerate for aarch64 wheels. Failing tests in `textgen/serve` that import `tokenizers`
Maria C: ugh, saw that. Fail looks like wheel binary mismatch: `ImportError: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory` in tokenizers C bindings
Alex H: Repro locally with py3.10 in the macos-latest container too. stacktrace points at `tokenizers._tokenizers` extension load
Jordan P: sec-bot posted CVE earlier for tokenizers? @sec-bot any details?
sec-bot: CVE-2025-XXXX: tokenizers < 0.15.3 has unsafe deserialization in `Token.from_bytes` when input is crafted. Severity: Medium. Patched in 0.15.3. Link: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-XXXX
Maria C: This is weird because our pyproject has `tokenizers = "^0.15.0"` so lock pulled 0.15.2 -> vulnerable. But the CI runtime error is different (binary load), likely manylinux wheel mismatch from the new lock.
Eli T: Could be pip pulled a manylinux2014 wheel that isn't compatible with our docker base image. We saw similar when upgrading `transformers` where manylinux tags changed.
Samira K: What's the constraint policy? Do we prefer pinning to safe patch (0.15.3) or rolling back to previously vendored wheel?
Alex H: Priority: 1) restore green CI, 2) remove vulnerable tokenizers version, 3) ensure private deploys don't pull vulnerable wheel. Proposal: open hotfix branch that pins `tokenizers==0.15.3` in `poetry.lock` and add an explicit `constraints.txt` for pip-install step used in Private deploy images.
Jordan P: Sounds good. Also need to check `transformers` minor bump: some 4.x -> 4.y pulled new tokenizers API that requires different build flags. I can try reproducing wheel mismatch locally with `pip debug --verbose`
Maria C: If we pin, we should also update SBOM and the KMS/audit policy notes. Compliance team needs an audit log of the change for Dedicated/Private customers. @Eli T can you add an audit entry when we cut the release?
Eli T: Yep. I'll add a release note and an audit log event. Also we should add an RBAC note: only infra-release role can push the hotfix to Dedicated.
Samira K: CI workaround: in the short term add `--no-binary :all:` to the tox env to force source build for tokenizers? That might be slow, but will confirm if it's wheel mismatch vs import error.
Alex H: Tried `--no-binary` locally, it fails earlier during build (Rust toolchain missing). So forcing source build in CI isn't great.
Jordan P: OK. I'll try regenerating lock on a linux container matching our build image then push a hotfix lockfile. If lock still pulls 0.15.2, we'll force `tokenizers==0.15.3` in pyproject and run `poetry lock --no-update` to rewrite lock entries.
Maria C: Also a follow-up: `fastapi` and `starlette` pinned in many services. Do we need to worry? Not directly for this CVE, but some apps failed to start when tokenizers import error bubbled up. Let's scan services that depend transitively on `transformers`/`tokenizers` and list owners.
Alex H: I've started a quick grep across repos: `infra/ai-services`, `apps/semantic-search`, `sdk/redwood-llm` -> owners tagged. Will post a short list in the PR description.
sec-bot: Note: Add to vuln-triage board and set priority P1 if vulnerable package is in production images.
Alex H: Action items:
- Jordan: attempt lock regen on linux image + open PR with hotfix branch that pins `tokenizers==0.15.3` (branch: hotfix/tokenizers-0.15.3) (ETA 2h)
- Maria: run dependency scan across services and add owners to PR (ETA 3h)
- Eli: prepare audit log entry + RBAC note for Dedicated release (ETA EOD)
- Samira: prepare CI patch to use a wheel caching step and fail CI on vulnerable versions (ETA tomorrow)
Jordan P: opened draft PR #4125 with initial lockfile changes and CI reproducer logs. CI still failing on macos runner due to wheel binary mismatch, but linux CI passes with pinned 0.15.3 wheel. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4125
Alex H: Great. Maria, can you confirm the vulnerability is fixed in 0.15.3 and there are no downstream changes in `transformers` that break our runtime?
Maria C: Confirmed: changelog shows CVE fix only. Ran our small eval harness against `transformers` with `tokenizers==0.15.3` — no behavior regressions.
Eli T: After PR merges, I'll coordinate a canary deploy to Dedicated pool and monitor logs for `ImportError` or rust runtime issues. If we see regressions, we can fallback to earlier pinned container with vendored wheel.
Samira K: Also let's add an explicit check in our CI vulnerability job to reject tokenizers < 0.15.3 and fail the build fast. I'll add a small script that reads `poetry.lock` and errors if found.
Alex H: Sounds like a plan. Thanks all. I'll merge the hotfix once CI green on linux and audit entry is ready. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: build master / unit-tests (linux) — 12m ago — ❌ failing: `textgen/serve` import error on macos runner.
Maria C: leaving a note to ops: after we merge we should trigger image rebuild for Private and Dedicated so customers don't pull older wheel during rollout.
Alex H: will file the image rebuild ticket after merge.
